entry.dc:title: VALEP - the world's first long distance phosphate concentrate slurry pipeline.
entry.dc:creator: Fister L.
entry.dc:description: The VALEP pipeline, which started operation in March 1979, is the world's first long distance slurry ppeline to transport phosphate concentrate. The 120 kilometer line is northwest of Rio de Janeiro, in the state of MinasGeras, Brazil; it connects the mine and concentrator near Tapira with a fertilizer complex near Uberaba. The 9 inch line is designed to transport 2.0 million dry metric tonnes of phosphate per year (dmtpy) at 61% solids by weight. As initial capacity of the concentrator is 900,000 dmptpy, batchimg of slurry alternately with water will be required until the concentrator is expanded. The particle size distribution of the slurry is minus 65 Tyler mesh, with approximately 35 percent of the solids minus 325 Tyler mesh. The entire project includes an open pit mine, a concentrator, a pipeline with pump station and orifice station, and terminal facilities at the fertilizer complex. (A)

entry.dc:title: Dust Control in Open Pit Mines.
entry.dc:creator: Pchelkin Y.
entry.dc:description: Dust conditions in open pit coal mines are considered in relation to different technological processes of mining. Results of laboratory investigations and industrial experiments regarding dust control when mining coal by rotary excavators and when transporting the mass of rock by trucks are presented. The investigaitons were carried out, inter alia, at the ″Korkinski″ open pit mine, 420 m deep, in South Yakutia, and other places. As a result, new dust-binding substances, ″Universin-A″ and ″Universin-B″ , satisfying all physico-chemical and production requirements have been developed. They belong to liquid compounded bitumens.

entry.dc:title: In-situ induced-polarization and magnetic susceptibility measurements-Yerington mine
entry.dc:creator: Hunter Ware G.
entry.dc:description: The Yerington Mine is an open pit mine of 'porphyry-copper' type. Primary mineralization (quartz veins, Cu-Fe sulfides, magnetite, and silicate alteration) is closely associated with a complex sequence of quartz monzonite porphyry intrusives. This primary mineralization is disrupted by subsequent alteration and faulting. The fault block containing the deposit has been rotated almost 90 degrees to the west; plan maps represent pretilt vertical sections. Almost one mile of pretilt vertical extent is exposed in the pit. Geologic observations may be taken only upon mining advances at discrete intervals. Detailed in-situ induced-polarization response and magnetic susceptibility surveys, both taken upon the pit floor, have been used to supplement geologic mapping. These in-situ measurements reveal the distribution patterns of sulfides and magnetite and are useful in interpolation or correlation of contacts, faults, and mineralization patterns between mapped advances. In-situ induced-polarization (IP) response was measured using a Scintrex IPR-7 receiver. Observations were made on a 10 × 10-ft grid using a Wenner electrode array with 3 1/3-ft a-spacing. Susceptibility measurements were taken with a Bison model 3101-A bridge and an in-situ coil arrangement 5 ft in diameter. A composite area approximately 3000 by 500 ft, representing 15,000 data points, has been surveyed. Contoured maps of in-situ IP response and magnetic susceptibility reveal the mineralization pattern in detail. These maps correlate well with the geologically mapped distribution of porphyry intrusives and also indicate zones of sulfide remobilization and/or magnetite destruction, including fault zones. IP response and magnetic susceptibility correlate well with elemental assays, mineral abundances, ratios, and textures determined from bench mapping and pit floor samples. The spatial distribution of physical properties is extremely complex, which demonstrates the need for caution in the use of simple interpretative models. The abundance of magnetite locally present in this particular porphyry-copper environment is noteworthy.

entry.dc:title: WOODLAWN BASE METAL OPEN PIT MINE REACHES CAPACITY.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: 50 Woodlawn, near Canberra reached full milling capacity this year. The complex ore assays 1. 7 percent copper, 5. 5 percent lead, 14. 4 percent zinc, and 2. 9 ounces of silver per ton. The copper ore assays 1. 9 percent copper, 0. 1 percent lead, 0. 5 percent zinc, and 0. 25 ounce of silver per ton. The differential flotation mill has a designed throughput of 3,300 tons of ore per day and is operated in separate campaigns to treat the complex ore and copper ores.

entry.dc:title: Determination of the seepage characteristics of thick layers of heterogeneous soil mounds.
entry.dc:creator: Lavrinenko I.
entry.dc:description: For the first time in the U.S.S.R. , a tailings storage dump is being built on the surface of interior mounds of overburden of an operational open pit mine - at present the first stage of the mining operation, of 100 ha. surface area has been brought into operation. The spoil heaps comprise 40m. thick embankments of a heterogeneous mixture of sandy, loamy and clayey soils. To assess the amount of water percolation to be anticipated through the foundations of the embankments and drainage systems, it was essential to obtain the seepage characteristics of the soil mix. However, it was found that traditional methods did not give sufficiently reliable and consistent answers. Some in situ tests were therefore carried out using sections of the embankment each 100m. x 100m. in plan of different ages, i.e. 6 years, 4 years and 2 years. The tests were of several months duration and were confirmed by laboratory experiments. A formula was developed for assessing change in seepage coefficient with time in accordance with data obtained on site. (A.L.)

entry.dc:title: CERRO VERDE.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: This article describes mining, mineral processing and metallurgical operations at this Peruvian opencast copper complex, the first stage of which was placed onstream last year. The first stage involved the mining and treatment of the oxide ore in the Cerro Verde deposit for an eventual output of 33,000 tonnes/yr of electrolytic copper in the form of 99. 98% pure cathodes. The first section to come onstream in Stage 1 was the heap-leaching unit, in which acid solutions are sprayed over heaps of oxide ore. Other operations described include the open pit mine, processing plant, as well as solvent extraction and electrowinning facilities.

entry.dc:title: SURFACE TRIALS OF THE HYDROMINER.
entry.dc:creator: Summers D.A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Pap Presented at the Int Symp on Jet Cutting Technol
entry.dc:description: A longwall water jet mining machine called the Hydrominer has been developed at the University of Missouri-Rolla under a Bureau of Mines contract. The first design, referred to as Hydrominer One, has been extensively tested in an open pit mine and has clearly demonstrated that the working principle is viable. The second and greatly improved version, Hydrominer Two, has been built but has not as yet been tested extensively. This paper describes the test series and some of the changes which were required to better achieve the full productive potential of the Hydrominer concept.

entry.dc:title: BEAR CREEK FINDS WYOMING U3O8 ORE; THEN GETS MANY PERMITS FOR NEW MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Bear Creek Uranium is a joint venture between the Mono Power Company and the Rocky Mountain Energy Company with the latter as operator. The new mine and mill are 70 miles northeast of Casper, Wyoming. Bear Creek is one of the first companies to obtain all the necesary operating permits to develop a new open pit mine and operate a uranium processing mill. The mine and mill operations are described.

entry.dc:title: Gusino-Ozero Fuel and Energy Complex.
entry.dc:creator: Shchadov M.
entry.dc:description: The Gusino-Ozero district electric power station is the main link in the identically named fuel and energy complex presently being developed in the Buryat ASSR in East Siberia. The Kholboldzhino open pit mine now under completion is to produce 3 Mt of brown coal per annum. The deposit consists of seven gently sloping seams from 2 to 34. 7 m thick. The depth of the open pit is 285-325 m. The capacity of the Gusino-Ozero power plant, when completed in 1979, will be 1260 MW (comprising 6 power units of 210 MW each). So far three units have been put into operation.

entry.dc:title: RHEINBRAUN PRESERVES ENVIRONMENT.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: In the fall of 1978 stripping will start at what will become the largest open pit mine in the world. The Hambach pit of Rheinische Braunkohlenwerke AG will reach its full production rate by 1995 when 50,000,000 annual metric tons of brown coal will be mined. This mine is in the heart of the Rhineland. The approval of the decision to develop the Hambach pit was only granted after intensive investigations and studies. A much larger number of original forest areas is now to remain undisturbed. These will act as nuclei for natural regeneration and also as screens and buffers shielding the mining areas.

entry.dc:title: CONTINUOUS EXCAVATOR FOR SURFACE COAL MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Kay F.J.
entry.dc:description: A forward-rotating bucket wheel excavator designed to continuously fragment and load unshot coal has been tested in an open pit mine. In principle, the excavating wheels rotate faster than required for rolling contact with the surface so the buckets excavate, carry away material, and provide a tractive effort to aid in pulling the vehicle forward. Production rates of over 1,080 tons per hour (1,000 cubic yards per hour) have been achieved utilizing 510 hp, verifying projected fragmenting and loading cost savings of 80 percent over conventional methods. Furthermore, due to the uniformly small size of the coal excavated, additional savings in preparation plant costs are possible.

entry.dc:title: EXPANSION AT BRUNSWICK.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: The current expansion of Brunswick Mining & Smelting Corp. Ltd. at its base metal property in New Brunswick, Canada, is highlighted. The Canadian lead/zinc producer is expanding output from its underground mining operations and phasing out its open pit mine. The expansion program involves the sinking of a new shaft and underground development by novel methods.

entry.dc:title: ITERATIVE APPROXIMATION TECHNIQUES FOR MICROSEISMIC SOURCE LOCATION.
entry.dc:creator: Dechman G.
entry.dc:description: This report presents a method that was developed to adapt microseismic techniques for rock structure analysis to investigations of surface problems, such as slope failure in an open pit mine. The source location method and two derivative location algorithms are described in detail, and the speed and accuracy of the two algorithms are compared.

entry.dc:title: Optimal Control Algorithm for the Automated Operational Control System of an Open Pit Mine.
entry.dc:creator: Chernin E.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: The problem of synthesis of an optimal control algorithm, maximizing the profit, for the extremal automated operatioal control system (AOCS) for the transporation complex at an open pit mine is considered. A target function equation is obtained establishing the dependence of the profit variation on the main components. It is shown that the open pit mine AOCS may be considered as a control system, extremal as regards the profit value, with random drifting of the extremum. An algorithm ensuring the search for the optimal transport route according to the magnitude of the profit.

entry.dc:title: Project Solutions for Construction of the ″Vostochnyi″ Open Pit Mine.
entry.dc:creator: Vinnitskii L.
entry.dc:description: In addition to the two existing open pit mines in the Ekibastuz coal basin, a third one is to be constructed in the southern part of the basin. The open pit mine is to be 2. 8 km long and 0. 9 km deep. Coal reserves up to the depth of 350 m amount to 750 million t. Coal is to be mined by four ERP-2500 rotary excavators with the capacity of 2500 m**3/hr each. The annual output is to reach 20 million t. The total length of conveyor lines will amount to 11 km.

entry.dc:title: NOVA SCOTIA PLANS BIG COAL PROGRAMS.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Major developments in the Nova Scotia coal industry, including a new open pit mine in Pictou County, a series of drilling and exploration programs, and conversion of some Nova Scotia Power Corporation generating plants from oil to coal, have been announced by Premier Gerald A. Regan. The area of interest lies west of the town of Stellarton and includes seven seams of coal. A diamond drilling program carried out in co-operation with the Department of Regional Economic Expansion indicated a potential of up to 10,000,000 tons of coal accessible by open pit mining. Work will commence on engineering feasibility including detailed diamond drilling, hydrologic studies and design.

entry.dc:title: MAINTENANCE: AN ESSENTIAL SERVICE TO OPERATIONS.
entry.dc:creator: Webster L.
entry.dc:description: Located in the Highland Valley of B. C. 's interior the Lornex copper mine is a subsidiary of Rio Algom Mines Ltd. The open pit mine and concentration plant process a low-grade prophyry-type ore containing copper and molybdenum, as well as minor amounts of precious metals. A comprehensive program of preventive maintenance is carried out on all vehicles and equipment. Working round the clock, seven days a week, the crews service all items according to a predetermined schedule based on a 200-hour interval. Shovels and drills, however, get more frequent attention.

entry.dc:title: Comparison of Physical Methods of Control of Stability of Open Pit Mine Slopes.
entry.dc:creator: Turintsev Y.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: Results of investigations of the microseismic, pulse, and seismic methods to control open pit mine edge stability are set forth. Calculation formulas are presented and criteria of evaluation of the state of stress of slopes at a stage close to an equilibrium are derived. This permits timely development and application of antideformation measures.

entry.dc:title: GEOTECHNICAL FACTORS IN OPEN PIT MINE DESIGN.
entry.dc:creator: Pentz D.
entry.dc:description: This paper discusses those aspects of open pit mine design which are affected by geotechnical factors. Open pit mines in the context of this paper also includes open cast mines, where the ″ore″ is extracted and the waste material is immediately replaced or backfilled in the mined portion of the pit. Open pit mine design is a significant portion of project management and an attempt is made here to demonstrate where geotechnical engineering can be useful in improving mine design.

entry.dc:title: BLASTING VIBRATION LEVELS TRANSMITTED ACROSS FRACTURE PLANES.
entry.dc:creator: Berzal J.L.
entry.dc:description: This article presents experimental results obtained by means of field tests measuring vibration levels transmitted across a presplit fracture plane, across a natural fracture plane or joint in the rock mass, and across two artificial fracture planes with a distance between them of one metre. The vibration levels were compared with those assuming a solid rock mass. The tests were carried out in a Spanish open pit mine.

entry.dc:title: PROSPERITY RETURNS TO OLD GOLD CAMP WITH UMEX THIERRY MINE DEVELOPMENT.
entry.dc:creator: Fish R.
entry.dc:description: The main orebody at the Thierry mine is 15 million tons grading 1. 63 per cent copper. There is another 70 to 100 million tons of material grading 0. 4 per cent copper and 0. 2 per cent nickel which could become an open pit mine. The Thierry deposit ore minerals are chalcopyrite and pyrrhotite disseminated in a chlorite biotite schist and an ultrabasic intrusive. In addition to the copper values it also contains nickel, gold, silver, palladium and platinum.

entry.dc:title: The use of equivalent models in slope stability investigation
entry.dc:creator: Reik G.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Rock Mechanics and Mining Sciences and
entry.dc:description: The example of model tests carried out within the framework of a rock mechanics program investigating the stability of an open pit mine, is used to demonstrate the possible application of such experiments in the assessment of slope stability. If rock properties, rock structure and boundary conditions (in-situ stresses, water pressure etc.) are sufficiently well known, model tests can yield information on slope deformation and possible failure mechanisms that cannot be at present obtained by other methods. Tests carried out on two slope models simulating structural conditions at Cala mine, Huelva, Spain, have demonstrated the decisive influence of joint fabric on the mode of failure. © 1976.

entry.dc:title: COPPER OXIDE TO COPPER CATHODE: NEW CYPRUS JOHNSON OPERATION.
entry.dc:creator: Argall G.
entry.dc:description: Arizona's newest copper mine - Cyprus Johnson - is pollution free from pit to cathode copper. Cyprus Johnson has a low capital investment per ton of cathode copper, 1,140 (7,200,000 capital cost for 5,000 annual tons of copper metal). By comparison, the current capital required to bring a major porphyry copper open pit mine, flotation mill, smelter, and refinery into production is from 5,500 to 6,500 per ton of copper produced. Cyprus Johnson is mining an oxide ore body, so there is no sulphur problem. Copper metal has been produced since March 1975 by open pit mining, dump for leaching, LIX64N solvent extraction, and electrowinning. Johnson is also one of the few copper operations in the world where ore is mined and placed in leaching dumps for ultimate copper recovery by LIX-electrowinning.

entry.dc:title: DESIGNING 240,000 DAILY CUBIC METER MINING SYSTEMS.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: In the West German brown coal mining industry, developments have been characterized by the concentration of production in a limited number of large-scale open pit mines. This situation led to the development of bucket wheel excavators, belt conveyor systems and stackers of the 110,000 bank cubic meter per day capacity class. A new class of open pit mining equipment, capable of handling 240,000 bank cubic meters per day, is now required for the intended production increase at Fortuna, Garsdorf as well as for the handling of 320,000,000 bank cubic meters and tons per year from a depth of nearly 500 meters in the future Hambach open pit mine. These volumes correspond to a handling rate of 5. 3 cubic meters (bulk) per second. The main design and operating characteristics of the new generation of 240,000 daily cubic meter excavator and handling systems are described.

entry.dc:title: Deformations of a Slope Excavated in the Valdarno Overconsolidated Clay.
entry.dc:creator: D'elia B.
entry.dc:description: The authors describe a study which used inclinometer measurements to determine the displacements of a clay slope during and after its excavation at the S. Barbara open pit mine. The influence of the structures present in the Valdarno overconsolidated clay on the time-dependent deformation process of the excavated slope is discussed. The finite element method was used in an analysis of the slope deformation immediately upon excavation, assuming a linear and nonlinear behavior of the clay. The analyses show the importance of a correct evaluation of the geotechnical properties of the soil.
